newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Ailing Thai finance firms funding woes grow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ailing Thai finance firms funding woes grow.

text.p: Thailand's troubled finance sector woes deepened as they faced mounting liquidity problems, with viable funding options becoming limited and liquidity drying up locally, analysts and trade sources said on Friday.
Declining confidence in the sector and central bank measures to counter currency speculation now threatened to push funding costs well above lending rates for many firms, they added.
Bank of Thailand controls since mid-May, which limit offshore access to the baht, have seen the development of a new and informal two-tier onshore and offshore dollar/baht markets.

The controls, imposed after the latest speculative attack on he embattled baht, have seen the currency rally to a 13-year high against the dollar offshore, as speculators scrambled to cover short baht positions, forex dealers said.
But the measures also threaten to slow foreign capital inflows and tighten domestic liquidity, analysts said.
Combined with the perceived risks attached to some weaker finance firms, overnight lending rates offered to them have recently risen above 20 percent, traders said.
For companies linked to commercial banks the situation is less serious, but for some others among the 90 firms in the sector, funding options are now increasingly limited, analysts said.
Fund raising through new share issues has been curtailed by a plunging local stock market, now at eight-year-lows.
Many finance firms, hit by lower revenues and declining asset quality as Thai economic growth slows, are unable to issue domestic bonds or secure bank loans at competitive rates, analysts said.
The bills of exchange market, an important source of finance firm funding, has been hard hit by the new capital controls, traders said.
"The market is very quiet since early May when the Bank of Thailand stopped sales of bills of exchange to foreigners in baht," said a fixed income trader at Nithipat Capital Plc.
As cost effective funding options dry up, finance firm competition to raise promissory note deposits has heated up, analysts said.
Such notes provided more than 70 percent of finance firm funding at the end of 1996, but lower confidence in the sector has seen a withdrawal of deposits by worried investors.
Figures released by troubled Finance One Plc showed promissory note funding declined to 29 percent of total funding in the first quarter 1997 against 61 percent of total funding at the end of 1996.
Top tier firms currently offer individuals about 12.25 percent interest on three month notes on deposits of two million baht. Rates at smaller firms are said to be highly negotiable.
To counter prohibitive rate rises, the central bank mooted the idea of forcing all finance firms to follow a set rate.

"We see this plan as carrying more risks than benefits...and likely to shift (funds) to the more secure fincos and banks, adding to the flight to quality already taking place," said Thaimex finance and Securities Plc in a recent report.
If rates are allowed to rise, the central bank, which has committed to support all ailing firms, will become more reliant on the central bank as a lender of last resort, analysts said.
How long that situation can continue and the capital controls remain in place is unclear, but, meanwhile, the outlook for most in the sector continues to worsen, analysts said,

"It is very hard for finance firms at the moment. If a firm is backed by a bank, problems are less severe, but right now it is becoming increasingly difficult for them generally," said a foreign analyst at a local broker.
